0.name: Bacterial Spot
0.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown and dry up; premature defoliation.
0.cause: Xanthomonas vesicatoria bacterium, spread by rain splash, overhead irrigation, and contaminated tools.
0.crop_impact: Severe defoliation reduces sun protection, causing fruit sunscald and significant yield reduction.

1.name: Early Blight
1.symptoms: Concentric target-like dark spots surrounded by yellow halos starting on lower older leaves.
1.cause: Alternaria solani fungus, favored by warm temperatures and high humidity/wet foliage.
1.crop_impact: Causes leaf drop, weakening the plant and reducing total fruit yield and quality.

2.name: Late Blight
2.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions with white moldy growth under humid conditions.
2.cause: Phytophthora infestans oomycete pathogen, spreading rapidly in cool, wet weather.
2.crop_impact: Highly destructive; can kill entire fields within days if left unmanaged.

3.name: Leaf Mold
3.symptoms: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with velvety olive-green to brown fungal growth underneath.
3.cause: Passalora fulva fungus, common in humid greenhouse or high-density tunnel environments.
3.crop_impact: Leaves wither and drop, reducing photosynthetic capacity and fruit development.

4.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
4.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark brown margins and greyish-white centers containing tiny black specks.
4.cause: Septoria lycopersici fungus, splashing up from infected soil onto lower leaves during rain or watering.
4.crop_impact: Progressive lower-to-upper defoliation exposing fruit to sunscald.

5.name: Spider Mites (Two-Spotted)
5.symptoms: Fine yellow/white stippling on upper leaf surface, delicate webbing on undersides, leaves turn bronze and dry up.
5.cause: Tetranychus urticae mites, thriving in hot, dry, dusty environmental conditions.
5.crop_impact: Rapid population growth causes leaf stippling, leaf drop, and severe plant stunting.

6.name: Target Spot
6.symptoms: Small brown water-soaked spots expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers and dark borders.
6.cause: Corynespora cassiicola fungus, encouraged by warm temperatures and prolonged leaf wetness.
6.crop_impact: Causes premature leaf drop and circular necrotic lesions on developing tomato fruit.

7.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
7.symptoms: Severe leaf curling (upward), yellowing margins, bushy stunted plant growth, and flower abortion.
7.cause: Geminivirus transmitted primarily by Bemisia tabaci (whiteflies).
7.crop_impact: Drastically reduces fruit set; plants infected early produce virtually no marketable fruit.

8.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
8.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic/mottling patterns on leaves, leaf distortion, blistering, and fern-like foliage.
8.cause: Tobamovirus spread mechanically through hands, tools, infected seeds, or plant contact.
8.crop_impact: Stunts growth, reduces yield, and causes uneven internal ripening of fruit.

9.name: Healthy
9.symptoms: Vibrant green foliage, sturdy stem growth, and absence of necrotic spots, leaf curling, or pest webbing.
9.cause: Optimal plant nutrition, ideal environmental conditions, and proper disease management.
9.crop_impact: High photosynthesizing efficiency leading to maximum crop yield and optimal fruit quality.
